title: A self-hosted LLM on Proxmox
summary: A local Qwen model and an embedding model on separate consumer GPUs, with a shared search service over the vault, the tracker, lab digests and repo docs.

stat.label: the lab agent answers from a model on my own GPU, with no hosted API key

sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: The budget had no API credit, so an internal agent could not keep calling a hosted API.

sections.heading: What I built
paragraphs: A local Qwen model and an embedding model on separate GPUs, each served by its own Ollama instance pinned to one card. A lab agent answers questions about the platform from the local model, and a search service that the agents share supplies the context.

The search service indexes the knowledge vault, the tracker, lab digests and repo docs. It embeds with the local embedding model and refuses to start without a caller token. Its tests use a fake embedder, so CI needs no route to the lab.

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: In my September audit, turning thinking off made the model roughly twice as fast, and the lab agent runs with it off. The model fits on one consumer card with its context.
The chat model is a mid-size Qwen3 and the embedding model is a small one, each on its own consumer GPU.
Today the lab agent answers questions about the platform from the vault, the tracker and repo docs on this model, with no hosted key behind it.

sections.heading: Trade-off
paragraphs: A thinking Qwen3 spends its output limit on reasoning, so the agent turns thinking off. The agent loop caps each reply length, the number of model turns and the total time. The last turn offers no tools, and a cut or empty answer is marked incomplete instead of being passed off as whole.

I audited every installed model on one question with thinking on and off: how many simultaneous disk failures a RAIDZ1 vdev survives. The Qwen3 model answered correctly both ways. Gemma 4 answered correctly only with thinking on.
What the agent stopped needing: an API gateway, a hosted key and a monthly spend cap. The gateway is retired.

sections.heading: What went wrong
paragraphs: The two newer Qwen3.5 models, a small one and a larger one, never closed their thinking block. They returned an empty answer with a clean status, so nothing in the call looked broken. I deleted both. A model has to be tested on the real question before it earns the default slot.
